_doc: Server-hosted services the code talks to (caches, search, mail, file transfer, queues, document stores, hosted logging) and the AWS managed service each can move to, with the code-side work per option. Read by aws_native.py. detect: packages = NuGet / assembly id regex (anchored, case-insensitive); client = regex for direct use of the client library on one code line (strings and comments are blanked first, except where client_in_strings is true); keyword = identifier fragment that names the service (used to find the repository's own wrappers and the call sites into them); config_keys = regex on configuration lines (assembly binding lines are ignored); config_values = regex on configuration values; legacy = client API that needs a rewrite whatever the target. targets: the first is the default unless the caller chooses another. change: config = settings, TLS and authentication only; client-swap = another client library behind the same wrapper; rewrite = the wrapper is rewritten for another service model; remove = the dependency is taken out. Hours are manual-equivalent (multiply by the AI factor named in factor: code or redesign, as for every other coding item): fixed = once per repository that uses the service; per_provider_file = each file that calls the client library directly (the wrapper); per_consumer_site = each code line that calls the wrapper; per_config_key = each configuration entry; legacy_per_provider_file replaces per_provider_file when the legacy API is found. Work that is not code (creating the AWS resource, networking, DNS, verified mail domains, data migration) belongs to DevOps and is not in these hours.

targets.work: Point the client at the ElastiCache endpoint; turn on TLS (ssl=true) and AUTH token or IAM authentication read from Secrets Manager; abortConnect=false and reconnect handling for failover; with cluster mode, check multi-key commands use hash tags.

EnyimMemcached 2.x is .NET Framework only: swap to EnyimMemcachedCore (or the ElastiCache cluster client for auto-discovery) behind the existing wrapper; point it at the cluster configuration endpoint; TLS if in-transit encryption is on.

targets.aws: Amazon ElastiCache (Valkey), one cache engine for Redis and Memcached users
targets.work: Rewrite the Memcached wrapper on StackExchange.Redis; keep the wrapper's method signatures; check expiry, serialisation and value-size behaviour at each call site.

targets.aws: Amazon ElastiCache (Valkey); AWS has no managed Aerospike
targets.work: Rewrite the Aerospike wrapper on StackExchange.Redis: namespace / set / bins become key prefixes and hashes, TTLs map directly, batch reads become MGET or pipelines, record-size limits and 'record too big' handling change, generation checks become WATCH or Lua; check each call site's result handling; load test.

targets.aws: Amazon DynamoDB (with DAX if latency matters)
targets.work: Rewrite the wrapper on AWSSDK.DynamoDBv2: table and key design, TTL attribute, 400 KB item limit (large values to S3), conditional writes for generation checks.

targets.aws: Keep Aerospike, self-managed on EC2 / EKS or Aerospike Cloud (not AWS native)
targets.work: Seed hosts, TLS and credentials only; the client library is already .NET Standard.

Swap NEST / Elasticsearch.Net for OpenSearch.Client / OpenSearch.Net (a fork of NEST 7.10, mostly namespace changes); SigV4 signing (OpenSearch.Net.Auth.AwsSigV4) or fine-grained access control; ILM rollover policies become ISM policies; index templates re-checked. Elasticsearch 8 clients (Elastic.Clients.Elasticsearch) need a real rewrite: use the high end.

Host email-smtp.<region>.amazonaws.com, port 587 with STARTTLS (EnableSsl = true), SES SMTP credentials from Secrets Manager; senders must be verified identities. System.Net.Mail.SmtpClient still works on .NET 10 but is not recommended: MailKit if the wrapper is touched anyway.
Send through the SES v2 API with the task's IAM role (no SMTP password); configuration sets for bounces and complaints through SNS; attachments as raw MIME.

targets.aws: AWS Transfer Family (SFTP / FTPS endpoint over Amazon S3 or EFS)
targets.work: Keep the SFTP client code; new endpoint, host key and user key pair from Secrets Manager. Plain FTP must become SFTP or FTPS (Transfer Family serves FTP only inside a VPC). Only for servers the client runs: a partner's SFTP server stays where it is.

targets.aws: Amazon S3 directly (AWSSDK.S3), for internal file hand-offs
targets.work: Replace upload / download / list / delete with S3 calls under the task's IAM role; S3 event notifications instead of polling a folder.

targets.aws: Amazon S3 behind a small storage interface
targets.work: Put file reads and writes behind one storage interface with an S3 implementation; pre-signed URLs where users download; no shared folder needed by any container.

targets.aws: Amazon EFS (Linux containers) or FSx mounted into the task
targets.work: Mount the file system into the task and point the path settings at the mount; Windows UNC paths become Linux paths.

Current MongoDB.Driver (the 1.x legacy API with MongoServer / MongoCollection<T>.Insert must be rewritten); TLS with the Amazon RDS CA bundle; retryWrites=false; check unsupported operators and index types.
Delete the wrapper, its packages and settings once the client confirms the store is unused in every environment.
amqps endpoint (TLS on 5671), broker user from Secrets Manager; no code change beyond the connection factory.
Publish to SNS topics / SQS queues and consume with long polling; dead-letter queues for retries; exchanges and routing keys become topics and subscription filters.
Bootstrap brokers, TLS, and IAM authentication (aws-msk-iam-sasl-signer-net) or SASL/SCRAM from Secrets Manager.
Only where ordered replay is not needed: producers publish events, consumers poll queues; offsets and consumer groups disappear.
System.Messaging does not exist on .NET 10: send and receive through SQS (FIFO queues where order matters), dead-letter queue for poison messages.

services.label: Hosted log service (Loggly, Splunk, Sumo Logic, Papertrail)

targets.aws: Amazon CloudWatch Logs (stdout from the container, FireLens or the awslogs driver)
targets.work: Replace the hosted-log appender with structured stdout logging (or AWS.Logger.Log4net / Serilog CloudWatch sink); any code that calls the log service's API directly moves to the normal logger; dashboards and alerts are rebuilt by DevOps.

targets.aws: ASP.NET Core session on IDistributedCache backed by Amazon ElastiCache (or DynamoDB)
targets.work: AddStackExchangeRedisCache + AddSession; session values must be serialisable; data-protection keys shared across tasks.

AppFabric Caching is a Windows Server service with a .NET Framework client (verify the TFMs of the package in use): rewrite the cache wrapper on StackExchange.Redis or IDistributedCache; regions and tags have no Redis equivalent (use key prefixes); locking calls (GetAndLock / PutAndUnlock) become a Redis lock; TLS and AUTH or IAM from Secrets Manager.
Delete the wrapper, its packages and settings once the client confirms the store is unused in every environment.

Rewrite the cache wrapper on StackExchange.Redis or IDistributedCache; NCache features with no Redis equivalent (SQL dependencies, read-through/write-through providers, groups and tags) move into application code; TLS and AUTH or IAM from Secrets Manager.

targets.aws: NCache on EC2 Linux (keep the product; verify its Linux and .NET 10 client support)
targets.work: Point the client at the NCache servers on EC2; licence moves with the client; check the client package supports .NET 10 on Linux.
Delete the wrapper, its packages and settings once the client confirms the store is unused in every environment.

Rewrite the search wrapper on OpenSearch.Client; map the Solr schema to an OpenSearch mapping, analysers and synonyms; faceting becomes aggregations; re-index from the source of record. Check relevance with a sample of real queries.

targets.aws: Solr on EC2 or ECS (keep the product)
targets.work: Point SolrNet at the Solr endpoint on AWS; TLS and authentication; the cores and their config move with DevOps.
Delete the wrapper, its packages and settings once the client confirms the store is unused in every environment.

targets.aws: Amazon SES email receiving (to S3 and SNS / Lambda; verify the Region supports receiving)
targets.work: Replace the polling loop with SES receipt rules that store messages in S3 and notify through SNS or Lambda; parse the MIME from S3 with MimeKit; the receiving domain's MX record points at SES (DevOps).

targets.aws: Keep the mailbox (Exchange Online, Microsoft 365 or another host) and poll it from AWS
targets.work: Point the client at the mailbox host; OAuth instead of basic auth where the host requires it; credentials from Secrets Manager.

targets.aws: Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra; verify the CQL features in use)
targets.work: TLS with the Starfield certificate, SigV4 authentication plugin or service-specific credentials; consistency LOCAL_QUORUM; check unsupported CQL (some batch, UDF and materialized-view features).
Delete the wrapper, its packages and settings once the client confirms the store is unused in every environment.

targets.aws: RavenDB on EC2 or RavenDB Cloud on AWS (keep the product; verify hosting options)
targets.work: Point the client at the new cluster URLs; client certificate from Secrets Manager; check the client version supports .NET 10.

targets.aws: Amazon DocumentDB (rewrite to the MongoDB driver)
targets.work: Rewrite sessions, indexes and queries on MongoDB.Driver; RavenDB indexes and patching have no direct equivalent.
Delete the wrapper, its packages and settings once the client confirms the store is unused in every environment.

targets.aws: Couchbase on EC2 or Couchbase Capella on AWS (keep the product; verify hosting options)
targets.work: Point the client at the new cluster; TLS and credentials from Secrets Manager; client SDK 3.x for .NET 10.
Rewrite the data access for the new store; N1QL queries need redesign; key-value access maps to DynamoDB more directly.
Delete the wrapper, its packages and settings once the client confirms the store is unused in every environment.

targets.aws: Amazon Neptune with openCypher (verify the Cypher features in use)
targets.work: Use the Neo4j Bolt driver against Neptune's openCypher endpoint with IAM (SigV4) authentication; check unsupported Cypher (APOC procedures, some functions); Neo4jClient fluent queries need checking one by one.

targets.aws: Neo4j on EC2 or Neo4j Aura on AWS (keep the product)
targets.work: Point the driver at the new endpoint; TLS and credentials from Secrets Manager.

_doc_consumer: consumer_repo_fixed: a repository that only calls a wrapper living in a shared library still runs its paths against the new endpoint once (smoke test, settings). The wrapper's own work (fixed + per_provider_file) is counted with the library.
_doc_supersedes: supersedes_optional: generic items of modernization-assessment's optional_modernizations.json that this service's row replaces in the same repository (same service, priced from the wrapper and call sites instead of a flat per-file rate).
